We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}({t}^{2}+t)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}-2t+4)+{x}_{3}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-2) & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3} \\ (4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3})+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})t+({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+{x}_{3}{t}^{3} & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
4{x}_{2}-2\cdot 1=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained value into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}-2\cdot 1=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{1}=2.$
